div.p: iravukkuṟikkaṇ talaimakaṉ ciṟaippuṟamākat talaimakaṭkut tōḻi colliyatu.
What the confidante said to HER while HE was behind the hedge during the night tryst.

lg.l: kuṇakaṭaṉ mukanta toḷḷai vāṉam
paṇaikeḻu vēntar palapaṭait tāṉait
tōṉirait taṉaiya vāki valaṉērpu
kōṉimir koṭiyiṉ vacipaṭa miṉṉi
yurumura ṟatirkura ṟalaiip pāṉāṭ
perumalai mīmicai muṟṟiṉa vāyiṉa
vāḷilaṅ kaṭuvī tāay nāḷai
yiruveti raṅkaḻai yōṅkiya tīṇṭi
varuvatu mātō vaṇpari yunti
naṉiperum parappi ṉammūr muṉṟuṟaip
paṉiporu maḻaikkaṇ civappap paṉṉāṇ
muṉipaṭa rakala muḷkuvaṅ kollō
maṇimaruṇ mēṉi yāynalan tolaiyat
taṇivarun tuyarañ ceytō
ṉaṇikiḷar neṭuvarai yāṭiya nīrē.
The hollow clouds that drew [water] from the eastern sea,
rising clockwise, being like the hide [shields] put in rows
of the king’s army with many weapons, equipped with large drums,
flashing so as to split [the sky], like banners held erect by a staff,
showering [rain] with a shaking voice, thunder rolling, at midnight,
they have become full-grown on the height of the big mountain.
Tomorrow, spreading nearby blossoms shining with light,
gripping the pretty poles of large bamboo that have become high,
won’t it come along the river with liberal motion,
in the huge expanse by the front ghat of our village,
– so that [our] rain eyes fighting with tears become red, many days,
so that [our] hateful affliction departs, will we enter? –
the water that played on the long mountain, decoratively shining,
of him who caused [this] misery difficult to appease,
so that the choice beauty of [our] sapphire-like bodies is lost?
